title: Lesion atlas: arch and vessels (right arch, double arch, aberrant subclavian, ductus)

items.question: What does the normal three-vessel-and-trachea view show?
options: Two arches of similar size forming a V to the left of the trachea
Two arches forming a U around the trachea
A single arch to the right of the trachea
items.explanation: Normally the ductal and aortic arches form a V to the left of the trachea.

items.question: The arches form a U around the trachea and oesophagus. What is this the key sign of?
items.explanation: A U shape instead of a V is the key sign of a vascular ring.

items.question: A vascular ring is suspected. What must then be excluded?
options: Aberrant subclavian arteries and a double aortic arch
items.explanation: With a suspected vascular ring, aberrant subclavian arteries and a double arch should be excluded.

items.question: Why does a vascular ring matter for the newborn?
options: It carries an increased risk of tracheal anomalies, including complete tracheal rings
It always needs surgery on the first day
It causes heart failure before birth
items.explanation: A vascular ring carries an increased risk of tracheal anomalies.

items.question: A pulmonary artery sling is diagnosed. Where should the baby be delivered?
options: Where assisted ventilation is available if needed
Anywhere; a sling has no airway relevance
Only where fetal surgery is possible
items.explanation: A sling may coexist with airway abnormalities; delivery should be where assisted ventilation is available.

items.question: Which tool shows an aberrant right subclavian artery behind the oesophagus more clearly?
options: Pulsed-wave Doppler of the umbilical artery
items.explanation: An isolated aberrant right subclavian artery is seen more clearly with colour Doppler.

items.question: A pulsatile, tortuous duct is seen at 37 weeks. What is the usual course?
options: It mostly closes spontaneously, with a low risk of rupture or compression
It needs delivery within a day
items.explanation: Ductal aneurysm mostly closes spontaneously with low risk, though it is associated with connective tissue disorders.

items.question: Isolated ductal constriction is found. Which history should you ask about?
options: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and certain foods or herbal teas
items.explanation: Constriction is associated with cyclo-oxygenase inhibitors and certain foods or herbal teas.

items.question: What can isolated ductal constriction lead to?
options: Right heart failure, hydrops, and persistent pulmonary hypertension after birth
items.explanation: Isolated constriction can lead to right heart failure, hydrops and PPHN.
